title: What 100 Economies Have Taught Us About Climate and Development
gist: Paschal Donohoe reviews lessons from the World Bank Group's Country Climate and Development Reports, now covering 100 economies: start from national development priorities, help workers adapt, link investment to economic policy, and turn insights into action (42% of CCDR opportunities are now addressed via WBG financing). Next priorities are deeper private-sector engagement and putting nature on the balance sheet.

insights.claim: The World Bank Group's Country Climate and Development Reports now cover 100 economies, with São Tomé and Príncipe the latest addition.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: CCDRs form a broad pipeline of climate-development investment priorities.

insights.claim: The current El Niño illustrates how climate shocks quickly become development challenges, as drought hits crops and hydropower reservoirs and heavy rain destroys infrastructure.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Climate shocks transmit to food, power and infrastructure risk.
insights.locator: The current El Niño is a reminder

insights.claim: The CCDR principle, first set out for Türkiye in 2022, is to start with countries' own development priorities such as jobs, reliable energy, cleaner air and resilience.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Climate investment is framed through jobs and energy security rather than emissions alone.

insights.claim: Affordable renewable power lowers energy costs while reducing exposure to global price shocks and emissions, and resilient infrastructure costs less to maintain.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Energy-security arguments strengthen the case for renewables in import-dependent economies.

insights.claim: CCDRs identify country-specific leapfrog opportunities: off-grid solar for rural access in Niger, renewables and efficiency to cut imported fuel dependence in Fiji, low-carbon manufacturing for European market access in Morocco, and flood management to protect Thailand's role in manufacturing value chains.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Points to off-grid solar, low-carbon manufacturing and flood resilience as investable themes.

insights.claim: Solar growth in Pakistan and electric mobility in Nepal advanced faster than seemed realistic a few years ago because they aligned with national priorities and strong leadership.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Policy alignment can drive rapid clean-tech adoption in emerging markets.

insights.claim: Tajikistan will need 65,000 temporary workers for rooftop solar installations, with a risk of workforce oversupply as that demand tapers.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Clean-energy buildouts create boom-bust labor demand.

insights.claim: In Brazil, 88 percent of formal job switches occur within the same state, suggesting regional development strategies could help areas with concentrated at-risk jobs.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Low labor mobility amplifies regional transition risk.

insights.claim: Climate change is reshaping labor markets alongside demographic shifts, digitalization, AI and migration.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Multiple structural forces compound labor-market disruption.
insights.locator: Climate change is reshaping labor markets

insights.claim: 42 percent of CCDR opportunities are currently being addressed through World Bank Group financing.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: CCDRs are a leading indicator of WBG lending pipelines.
insights.quote: Today, 42 percent of CCDR opportunities are being addressed through World Bank Group financing.

insights.claim: CCDRs have moved climate issues from line ministries into finance and planning ministries; in Côte d'Ivoire the Council of Ministers endorsed the CCDR and tasked the Prime Minister's office with implementation.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Finance-ministry ownership raises odds that climate priorities are funded.

insights.claim: Donohoe argues climate-related technical knowledge is often stuck in silos or lacks political commitment and resources, so linking sector decisions to growth, jobs and fiscal stability is key to action.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Implementation capacity, not knowledge, is the bottleneck.
insights.locator: Experts often know how to use

themes.theme: Next priorities: private sector and nature

insights.claim: The next generation of CCDRs will draw more systematically on private-sector expertise to make recommendations more investable and responsive to market realities.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Expect more private co-investment angles in WBG climate diagnostics.

insights.claim: Future CCDR diagnostics will better integrate ecosystem services, nature-related financial risks and natural capital into economic analysis, building on reports for Cambodia, Peru, Ethiopia and Fiji.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Nature-related financial risk is entering sovereign policy analysis.
